The voice toggle's body is t("child.voiceWhy"), which says the browser may send audio to Apple or Google. That stops being true once Deepgram is configured, and the parent consented to a different processor. Change: keep a state `const [voiceLines, setVoiceLines] = useState<Key[] | null>(null)`. In an effect: `voiceStatus().then((s) => setVoiceLines(voiceDisclosure({ vendor: { in: s.stt && micSupported() ? "deepgram" : "browser", out: s.tts ? "elevenlabs" : "browser" }, allowed: true })))`, importing voiceStatus, voiceDisclosure and micSupported from "@/lib/voice". Render `body={voiceLines ? voiceLines.map((k) => t(k)).join(" ") : t("child.voiceWhy")}`. When the processor changes (the status flips to stt:true), the toggle should be turned off until the grown-up turns it on again. The family owner can store the vendor the consent was given for (for example `voiceConsentFor: "browser" | "deepgram"` in LearnerSettings) and treat consent as false when it differs.

followups: SKIPPED (reason given): limiting learners who aren't allowed voice to on-device voices only, one part of F17's suggested fix. Names are always removed before text reaches an online voice, and the new voice.source.browserRead line discloses that online voices exist. The rest is the tutor's reply text, which is not the child's personal information. Restricting to on-device voices would silently remove read-aloud for K-2 Spanish learners on Windows Chrome without a Spanish language pack, against plan 2.4 (K-2 replies read aloud). If counsel decides otherwise, filter pickVoice to localService when !allowed, and emit a 'speak' error when no local voice exists.

REMAINING RISK (F1): until M5 sessions exist, a determined script can still get a voice pass from /api/voice/status. Spend is now bounded by the Origin check, per-address budgets (12/8 a minute) and the daily ceiling, but those live in memory per instance and multiply across instances. Before setting KAIZEN_VOICE=vendor: (a) set usage or character caps on the ElevenLabs and Deepgram keys in their dashboards. (b) M5.7: move rate.ts and the daily counter to a shared store. (c) M5 (backend package): replace the body of lib/voice/server.ts voiceAllowed(req, kind, body) with a lookup of the stored consent record and age band for the signed-in session, and require that session in gate() in place of, or on top of, the voice pass. Callers don't change.

Deepgram grant JWTs carry usage:write on the core voice APIs. A stream opened with one can run as long as audio keeps arriving; a socket opened with an ElevenLabs single-use token likewise stays open while text keeps arriving. Neither can be capped from our side without a server relay (Vercel route handlers can't host WebSockets). The vendor key caps above are the backstop.

Latency bars (plan §6): converse and the session now report onMetric({ name: 'first-audio' | 'barge-in', ms, vendor }). Nothing collects these yet. Whoever wires the tutor should forward them to the ops/cost dashboard (M5.7), with no transcript or name attached. The unit tests prove the barge-in rule fires at 300 ms. End-to-end first audio in under 1.5 s can only be measured live, against the vendors.

Plan §2.4 / 6.4 (out of scope for this package): K-2 'tutor speaks first' and chants, and the UI for the two self-tests. The UI belongs in family settings. Run micSelfTest, then listenSelfTest on a voice() built for that screen; do not use a conversation's input, or the test's words would go to the tutor. The keys voice.selfTest.* are ready.

Echo detection is text-based, so one ambiguous case remains. If a learner repeats the last two or more words of the tutor's question within about a second of the tutor stopping, the reply can be set aside as echo. It is not lost: the session offers it back ('Did you say …?' with a send button). A single-word echo of the tutor's last word can still reach the tutor as a turn.

Spec gap closed inside owned paths: the exact wiring instructions for components/tutor/useVoice.ts + TutorChat.tsx and components/stage/useSpeech.ts + Stage.tsx are in 'requests'. lib/voice/index.ts also has an updated non-React usage sketch.

Also in requests: ChildSettings consent copy (child.voiceWhy) becomes false once Deepgram is configured, and consent should be asked again when the processor changes. The new env vars also need adding to apps/web/.env.example.

lib/types.ts: the doc comment on LearnerSettings.voiceInput still says 'browser speech recognition'. It now gates the microphone for any recognizer, at every age. The comment belongs to the owner of lib/types.ts.
